density.chosen_from: uniform over 1..4 per PLAN (the line-binding ceiling), from a stream seeded on (seed, 'density'); each line then draws its participation uniform over 1..3, and the end-rhyme pass binds free line ends on top (M-191)

end_rhyme.chosen_from: NOT A DRAW — each sung section's own `schemes[fn].rgs` re-realised at the line ends, so this consumes no seed entropy and the placement draw above is untouched. Three counts, never summed (doctrine 79): `added` groups emitted; `blocked` blocks whose ends the placement draw had already spent; `narrow` blocks whose lines cannot carry one more DISTINCT word.

execution.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

meter.chosen_from: 178 derived cycles (beats envelope [2, 12], slots envelope [5, 48]), measured BY DERIVATION ON THE DECLARED COORDINATE: 1 of 11 beats-per-line values, then 1 of 1 bars x subdivision factorisation(s) of 2 beats, then 1 of 1 groupings of 2. The line runs 2 beat(s) — at most the density band's ceiling, since a sung line carries at least one syllable a beat — and holds 8 slot(s), at least the band's floor. Both ends are the same calibrated band in different units; the pair share follows from how many ways each beat count factorises. Unit is notation, never enforced

narrative.chosen_from: uniform over the 416 legal story line-ups of this shape (quality/narrative.py, M-121; the count is exact and the draw is entropy-last)

pattern.chosen_from: generated grammar: 22 cell types x 1..7 cells under the drawn total and declared brief, optional intro/outro/coda, roster 20 of 22 functions

placements.measure: uniform per MEMBER over the pool; per member and not per group because 8 of the 77 registered schemas anchor one member at each end of a word
placements.token_ceiling_from: the smaller of the floor's measured tokens-per-line floor 7.00 and this plan's own shortest line (5 syllable(s) after its pickup) less one for the last word — a plan asks for the n-th word only where BOTH the calibration and this meter say a line carries that many

relations.chosen_from: NOT DRAWN — the writer declared --relation and a declared coordinate is carried, never sampled over (M-55)

execution_limits.basis: registry span enumeration; no phonological bucket pruning assumed
execution_limits.scope: English lines at or below the declared density ceiling; no latency/RSS guarantee

plan.title: The Greenhouse Clock
plan.writer_brief:
Write a song: 28 lines, 5 sections, in this order:
  [CHORUS — 7 lines — 7 bars of 2/4, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 5 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [BRIDGE — 3 lines — 3 bars of 2/4, quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 7 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 9 lines — 9 bars of 2/4, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 5 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 7 lines — 7 bars of 2/4, three-quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 5 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [OUTRO — 2 lines — 2 bars of 2/4, quarter-beat pickup]
      up to 7 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
Feel: 2/4 grouped 2.

  lines 1.T4 & 2.T3 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme

  lines 9.T1 & 10.T2 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme

  lines 13.T3 & 15.T3 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme

  lines 27.headrime & 28.endword stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 27.T3 & 28.head stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 4 & 7 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 12 & 17 & 18 stand in ASSONANCE — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
Story plan (one job per sung section; each enters from the section before it as stated):
  CHORUS1 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to
  BRIDGE1 flips the reading of everything before it — set beside (connection unstated) CHORUS1
  VERSE1 is a compressed verdict on what has happened — after BRIDGE1
  CHORUS2 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — because of VERSE1
  OUTRO1 is the leave-taking — the walk home — set beside (connection unstated) CHORUS2
Every chorus after the first repeats the first chorus word for word, line for line.
Line 1 is the hook — make it the line someone leaves humming.
Where a binding sits (a bare line number is its end word, read as a rhyme span):
  T2: word 2, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T1: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T3: word 3, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  endword: the end word, read whole, from its first syllable
  T4: word 4, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  headrime: the first word, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  head: the first word, its first syllable — the head-rhyme / alliteration reading
